recent_articles.title: Tight security for Vijay’s visit to Tiruchi today - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, is scheduled to arrive in Tiruchi on Monday for a thanksgiving ceremony at St. Joseph’s College ground.  A large number of **TVK** cadres are expected to attend the event, which will feature a speech by Mr. Vijay thanking voters for their support. Over 2,500 police personnel from various districts have been deployed for security arrangements, including traffic diversions and barricades at vantage points. The event is limited to 5,000 attendees with entry passes, excluding pregnant women, children, schoolchildren, senior citizens, and people with disabilities.

recent_articles.title: Worth examining Vijay’s appeal to children to convince adults to vote for him, says judge citing personal anecdote - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Justice G.R. Swaminathan** of the Madras High Court presided over a case involving an appeal by **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to children to vote for his party, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  Senior counsel **S. Muralidhar**, representing TVK, argued that the petition was based on news reports and urged the court to adjourn the matter so he could study it in depth.  **N.R. Elango** and **S.R. Rajagopal**, representing DMK and AIADMK respectively, countered by stating their clients were accused of voter bribery and should be dealt with through election petitions. The case was adjourned until July 1, 2026, for counter affidavits.

recent_articles.title: Former AIADMK MLA from Jayamkondam joins TVK - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **J.K.N. Ramajeyalingam**, former **AIADMK** MLA, joined the ruling **TVK** party on Friday.  **S. Ravi**, another former **AIADMK** MLA, also met with **TVK** leader and Water Resources Minister **N. Anand** to discuss joining the party. Pugazhendhi, a former **AIADMK** functionary, also met with **Anand** for a courtesy call. The reasons for Ramajeyalingam's decision include the "popular mandate" for **C. Joseph Vijay**, the **TVK** chief, and **Palaniswami's** attempts to form a government.

recent_articles.title: Dhinakaran slams TVK govt. for not launching ‘Singa Penn’ special police wing - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **T.T.V. Dhinakaran**, general secretary of the **Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK)**, criticized the **Tamil Nadu** government for its delay in establishing the Singapenn special police wing to address violence against women. He questioned **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's** commitment to women's safety after he had previously approved the wing's formation during his swearing-in ceremony. Dhinakaran also expressed concern about the state's current government, suggesting that it lacks the necessary leadership and integrity to ensure public safety.

recent_articles.title: Puthiya Tamilagam demands closure of all Tasmac outlets across the State - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Puthiya Tamilagam**, a Tamil Nadu political party, urged the state government to implement total prohibition, close all Tasmac outlets and bars, and address alleged corruption in the liquor trade. The party also expressed concern over rising crime rates and social degradation linked to alcohol consumption.  The party welcomed the emergence of a third political force in Tamil Nadu politics but cautioned against multiple power centers within the government.

recent_articles.title: Session to focus on the rise of the TVK at The Hindu Huddle - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: In Tamil Nadu, the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** secured an unexpected victory in the Assembly elections on May 4th, winning nearly 35% of the vote and securing 108 seats. This unprecedented result marks a significant shift from traditional Dravidian politics, with the TVK utilizing online campaigns and targeted messaging to reach younger demographics like Gen Z. The party's success is attributed in part to K.G. Arunraj, a former civil servant who joined the party in June 2025 and played a key role in its campaign strategy.

recent_articles.title: What Tamil Nadu CM Vijay really needs to see at Fort St. George - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, visited **Fort St. George** last week but did not see all of its historical sites. The Fort is facing issues with poor general upkeep, including piles of trash and a neglected moat. These problems are visible throughout the precinct, highlighting the need for improvement to preserve this historic enclave.

recent_articles.title: A new brand of politics in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, leader of the **Tamilaga Vetri Kazhagam (TVK)**, has emerged as a significant force in Tamil Nadu politics following the 2026 Assembly elections.  His victory marks the first time a Christian has become Chief Minister in the state's history and challenges the long-standing dominance of the **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)** and **All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK)** parties, who have alternated power for over half a century.  The rise of TVK presents a new dynamic in Tamil Nadu politics.

recent_articles.title: CM Vijay to fly to New Delhi on Wednesday, to call on PM Modi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, will travel to New Delhi on Wednesday to meet **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**.  He plans to discuss issues including financial matters and the **Mekedatu** reservoir project with **Modi**.  **Vijay** is also expected to meet with Union Ministers and may meet with **Rahul Gandhi**.

recent_articles.title: Opposition parties criticise CM Vijay over a spate of crimes across Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, and other Opposition leaders criticized **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, over a recent surge in crimes across the state. They questioned his response to the issue, demanding explanations for measures taken to protect women and children.  They also criticized his lack of action compared to his pre-election rhetoric on women's safety.

recent_articles.title: Ex-VCK MLA threatens to leave party over its support for TVK - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **VCK** leader **Thol. Thirumavalavan** is facing criticism from former MLA **Panaiyur Babu**, who has expressed his desire to leave the party due to perceived ideological inconsistencies and leadership style.  **Sinthanai Selvan**, VCK general secretary, urged Mr. Babu to reconsider his decision, emphasizing the leader's dedication to social equality.

recent_articles.title: Mekedatu dam issue: CM tells officials to pursue legal action - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** instructed officials to pursue legal action regarding the Mekedatu dam issue after a meeting with experts and legal luminaries on Monday. The meeting, attended by **Ministers N. Anand**, **Aadhav Arjuna**, and **R. Nirmalkumar**, and senior officials, considered the Supreme Court's November 2025 ruling that only the Central Water Commission could determine if the project complied with previous judgments.  The review petition against this verdict was dismissed in December 2025, prompting **Vijay** to direct expedited legal action.

recent_articles.title: Vijay should strongly oppose Mekedatu dam plan: Seeman - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Seeman**, chief co-ordinator of **Naam Tamilar Katchi**, criticized **D.K. Shivakumar**, Karnataka's deputy Chief Minister, for his statement that Tamil Nadu does not have the right to oppose the Karnataka government's plan to build a dam at Mekedatu across the Cauvery river.  **Seeman** called the statement arrogant and said it indicated an attempt by **Karnataka** to claim exclusive ownership over the Cauvery river water rights. He urged **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to register strong opposition to the project.

recent_articles.title: BJP tried to stitch coalition govt. in Tamil Nadu with DMK and AIADMK on election result day: Congress MP Manickam Tagore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** MP B. Manickam Tagore accused **DMK** leader Udhayanidhi Stalin of attempting to form a coalition government with the **AIADMK** to prevent TVK president C. Joseph Vijay from becoming Chief Minister.  He claimed that the **DMK**'s actions were orchestrated by the **BJP**, and that they will soon strike an understanding with the party, potentially leading to DMK MPs abstaining from voting against the BJP-led government in Parliament.  **Girish Chodankar**, Congress's in-charge for Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, responded to the accusations by stating that the attacks on the Congress should not be directed at the people of Tamil Nadu who voted.

recent_articles.title: TVK government will fall one day, says M.K. Stalin - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M.K. Stalin**, leader of the **DMK**, criticized the **TVK** government, led by Chief Minister **C. Joseph Vijay**, for its dependence on other parties for support and alleged attempts to split the AIADMK.  He compared the public's interest in the new party to a child's fascination with a toy, predicting that it would fade quickly. **Stalin** also highlighted his government's achievements over the past five years as evidence of improved governance.

recent_articles.title: Coalition government here to stay in Tamil Nadu like Kerala, says Kader Mohideen - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K.M. Kader Mohideen**, president of the **Indian Union Muslim League (IUML)**, stated that Tamil Nadu has formed a coalition government similar to Kerala and that it will continue in the future. He attributed this success to the DMK's ability to secure votes from the Muslim community, which he believes was crucial for their victory.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new leader of Tamil Nadu politics, is credited with initiating this change.

recent_articles.title: Ponraj gets anticipatory bail over remarks on TVK women supporters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V. Ponraj**, a political commentator, has been granted anticipatory bail by the **Madras High Court** in two criminal cases related to derogatory remarks against women supporters of **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** and the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**. The court imposed conditions requiring him to appear before police twice a week and once a week, as well as refrain from threatening witnesses or tampering with evidence.  The judge acknowledged the intent behind Ponraj's statements but granted bail due to his strong ties to society and low risk of absconding.

recent_articles.title: Jana Nayagan leak case: Madras High Court denies bail to six accused - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Madras High Court** denied bail to six individuals who shared and watched the leaked film "Jana Nayagan" before its official release.  **Justice R. Sakthivel** dismissed all bail petitions after the prosecution argued that the illegal viewing of the movie by millions constituted a serious offense.

recent_articles.title: Seven MLAs from Chennai find place in Tamil Nadu cabinet: highest in recent years - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** and seven other ministers from Chennai constituencies were sworn in on Thursday, marking a significant representation for the city in the new cabinet.  This is one of the highest contributions to the current cabinet from **Chennai**, with many top leaders from the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) contesting from the city and becoming ministers.

recent_articles.title: After CM Vijay’s order to revive Amma Canteens, AIADMK hopes for comeback of other legacy schemes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **AIADMK** functionaries have called for the revival and strengthening of several welfare schemes implemented during the party's previous tenures, including Amma Canteens, Amma Salt, Cradle Baby scheme, Amma Scooters, and 'Gold for Thali'. They also criticized the **Tamil Nadu** government's handling of government properties and alleged that several welfare programs initiated by the previous AIADMK regime have been discontinued or poorly implemented.  These criticisms were made during a meeting with the newly elected government led by **C. Joseph Vijay**.

recent_articles.title: DMK faces a challenge as allies set to join TVK government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DMK**, the Secular Progressive Alliance's leader since 2017, has lost most of its pre-poll allies.  The party is now left with only **MDMK** and **Manithaneya Makkal Katchi**, who contested on its Rising Sun symbol. Additionally, the DMDK remains loyal to the TVK government. The Congress abandoned the DMK after the Assembly polls and joined Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's Cabinet on Thursday, while the IUML and VCK are expected to join the Ministry on Friday.

recent_articles.title: Historic shift: Vijay’s Cabinet marks Tamil Nadu’s best SC representation till date - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has appointed seven members from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community to his Cabinet. This marks a significant increase in SC representation compared to previous Cabinets.  Political analyst Stalin Rajangam believes this is a positive step towards inclusivity and sets a benchmark for future governments. However, Punitha Pandiyan, former Vice President of the Tamil Nadu SC/ST Commission, argues that celebrating this development trivializes SC politics.

recent_articles.title: 22 Ministers aged below 50: Cabinet signals generational shift in Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government's Cabinet has seen a significant shift in age composition, with the 2026 TVK Cabinet featuring the youngest average age among the three governments examined.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of this government, is 51 years old and his cabinet features the youngest Ministers at just 28 and 29 years old. The 2026 TVK Cabinet has nine Ministers in their 30s, followed by a senior tier of seven Ministers in their 50s, three in their 60s, and only one in the 70-80 age bracket.  This contrasts with the 2021 DMK Cabinet which was heavily dominated by older leaders.

recent_articles.title: ‘Barring elected representatives, TVK members not to go for inspections’: Minister Arunraj - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** general secretary **K.G. Arunraj**, Minister for Health and Family Welfare, clarified that only elected representatives are authorized to conduct inspections.  His statement followed criticism of a woman claiming to be from the party's medical wing inspecting the Government Hospital in Sankarankovil, as instructed by **TVK** president **C. Joseph Vijay** and general secretary **N. Anand**.

recent_articles.title: CM’s appeal to kids for votes: Plea in Madras High Court seeks an inquiry by Election Commission - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: DMK, AIADMK, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Election Commission of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition has been filed in the Madras High Court, seeking an inquiry by the **Election Commission of India (ECI)** into allegations of electoral malpractice during the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. The petitioner, L. Vasuki, argues that **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay**'s appeal to children to vote for his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), constitutes "exploitation of minor children for electoral propaganda" and falls under the definition of corrupt practice.  The petition also cites a representation by the anti-corruption organization Arappor Iyakkam alleging that **DMK** and **AIADMK** members distributed cash to voters in certain constituencies. The court has sought responses from the **ECI** and **CEO** by May 29, 2026.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Cabinet expansion LIVE: Congress set to join Tamil Nadu’s first coalition government in decades - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** is set to expand his Cabinet with the oath of office for 23 new ministers scheduled for Thursday, May 21, 2026. Thirumavalavan**, leader of the VCK, and the **IUML** have been invited to join the Council of Ministers.

recent_articles.title: Kamal meets Vijay, submits 6 demands Tamil film industry’s development - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kamal Haasan**, founder of **Makkal Needhi Maiam**, met with **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to discuss the development of the Tamil film industry. He also requested the abolition of local body entertain taxes on movie tickets, a strong anti-piracy team, and a state-owned OTT platform for Tamil cinema.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Cabinet portfolios: CM Vijay to hold Home; Finance for Sengottaiyan; Aadhav Arjuna gets PWD - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, has announced the portfolios for his cabinet members. **Vijay** will oversee key departments including Home, Police, and IAS/IPS officers.  **N. Anand**, the deputy chief minister, will handle Rural Development and Water Resources. Other ministers have been assigned specific responsibilities in areas such as health, education, finance, and energy. The Governor has approved the recommendations.

recent_articles.title: Vijay opposes hike in fuel prices; seeks immediate rollback - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** criticized the recent fuel price hike, arguing that it disproportionately impacts low-income individuals and businesses.  He called for an immediate rollback of the increase, citing its negative effects on vehicle rentals, inflation, and manufacturing costs in the MSME sector. **Vijay** emphasized the hardship this will cause for those reliant on two-wheelers and mini buses, as well as those with loans tied to vehicle operation.

recent_articles.title: Remove import duty on cotton to ensure supply, CM Vijay urges Modi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, urged **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** to remove the 11% import duty on cotton to ensure raw material availability for the textile and apparel industry.  He cited the increase in cotton prices and yarn prices as a result of reduced production and increased trading activity, arguing that duty-free imports would help meet export commitments and protect jobs. The textile and apparel sector is a major employment generator, with **Vijay** emphasizing the government's responsibility to safeguard this sector.

recent_articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Fisheries Minister urges CM Vijay to ban bottom trawling - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sri Lanka’s** Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar urged **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to ban bottom trawling fishing, a practice prohibited in Sri Lanka since 2017, as he believes it is the root cause of ongoing conflict between the two states.  Chandrasekar expressed hope for diplomatic resolution and a meeting with Vijay, congratulating him on his recent election win. He praised Vijay's letter to **External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar** seeking intervention in the release of six Tamil Nadu fishermen arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy for fishing illegally in Sri Lankan waters. Chandrasekar stated that arrests are made because bottom trawling destroys marine resources and threatens livelihoods, emphasizing the need for a ban on this practice in Tamil Nadu to prevent future conflicts.

recent_articles.title: Tasmac shuts 150 outlets in three days; salesmen face challenges from customers - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** has ordered the closure of over 150 liquor outlets in Tamil Nadu, citing proximity to educational institutions and places of worship. The **Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited** (Tasmac) is responsible for identifying and closing these shops based on multiple criteria, including distance from public spaces and average sales figures.  The government has also issued a circular warning against selling liquor above the Maximum Retail Price (MRP), with officials instructed to conduct surprise inspections across the state.

recent_articles.title: Jayalalithaa’s picture still remains in my pocket: Sengottaiyan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K.A. Sengottaiyan**, Minister and TVK chief coordinator, stated that he still carries a photo of former Chief Minister **J. recent_articles.title: Nainar Nagenthran questions Vijay’s statement on minority government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nainar Nagenthran**, BJP State president, criticized **C. Joseph Vijay's** statement characterizing his government as "a government for minorities," questioning if it aims to suppress the majority. He accused the **DMK** of insulting Hindu sentiments while in power and demanded action against a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA who allegedly made derogatory remarks about Sanatana Dharma.  Nagenthran urged the party to prevent such statements from being made in the future.

recent_articles.title: Vijay govt. says it needs time to ‘restructure’ Magalir Urimai Thogai programme; funds to be disbursed soon - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Tamil Nadu** government announced it needs time to restructure the 'Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai' program, which provides a monthly grant of ₹1,000 to eligible women heads of families.  **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** had previously promised an increase to ₹2,500 per month under the new "Madhippumigu Magalir Thittam" program for women over 21 years old with family incomes below ₹2.5 lakh. The government stated that the May grant will be credited into beneficiaries' bank accounts soon.

recent_articles.title: DMK boycotts floor test; urges CM to continue with Dravidian model welfare schemes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, leader of the **Tamil Nadu** opposition, led his party members in a boycott of a confidence motion presented by Chief Minister **C. Joseph Vijay**.  The walkout occurred after **Stalin** stated that the majority did not vote for the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).

recent_articles.title: Scrap NEET-based admissions, allow States to fill up medical seats, Vijay appeals to Centre - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** urged the **Union government** to cancel the NEET-based admissions in medical courses and allow states to fill seats based on Class 12 marks.  Vijay cited multiple instances of NEET paper leaks, including a recent cancellation following investigations by law enforcement agencies, as evidence of the exam's flaws. He emphasized that the introduction of NEET has disadvantaged students from rural areas and socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds. The **NEET-UG 2026** was conducted on May 3, 2026, with over 22 million candidates appearing nationwide, including 140,000 from Tamil Nadu.

recent_articles.title: AIADMK legislature party splits vertically during trust vote in Tamil Nadu Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK)** legislature party in Tamil Nadu experienced a significant split during a trust vote.  **25 MLAs**, led by rebel leader S.P. Velumani, voted in favor of the motion moved by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay while 22 MLAs, led by AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami, voted against it. The division within the party highlights a growing rift between factions within the AIADMK.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly session LIVE: CM Vijay moves resolution seeking confidence vote - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, faces a floor test in the state assembly on May 13, 2026.  The test will require him to prove his alliance's majority after rebel AIADMK leaders led by former Ministers **S.P. Velumani** and **C.Ve. Shanmugam** announced support for his ruling **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**. The floor test comes as AIADMK MLAs from the faction supporting **Edappadi K. Palaniswami** have declared their intention to vote against the confidence motion.

recent_articles.title: Vijay urges Union Minister to secure the release of six T.N. fisherfolk arrested by Lankan Navy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamil Nadu** Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay requested the **Union Minister for External Affairs S. Jaishankar** to use diplomatic channels to secure the early release and safe repatriation of six Tamil Nadu fishermen arrested by the **Sri Lankan Navy** on May 10th for allegedly crossing the International Maritime Boundary Line while fishing. The fishermen, identified as Alex, Anthoni Rajan, Santhana Alocias, Arul They Britto, Albert, and Sahaya Selvashanu, were apprehended along with their fishing boat.

recent_articles.title: AIADMK rebel MLAs to back TVK in Tamil Nadu floor test - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, called on rebel AIADMK leaders **S.P. Velumani** and **C.Ve. Shanmugam** ahead of a floor test in the state Assembly. The rebels declared **Velumani** as the "AIADMK Legislature Party leader" but **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, the AIADMK general secretary, claimed he was the leader.  **O.S. Manian**, a senior leader supporting **Palaniswami**, stated that all 47 AIADMK legislators had signed a letter electing **Palaniswami** as the Legislature Party leader and that the rebels were attempting to lure MLAs. The rebels, who have accused **Palaniswami** of collaborating with the DMK, are seeking ministerial positions.

recent_articles.title: Quantum jump in followers of T.N. CMO’s social media handles after Vijay’s swearing-in - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister**, saw a significant increase in followers on his official social media accounts, particularly Instagram, following his swearing-in ceremony. The number of followers jumped from 4.56 lakh to 1.9 million within just two days.  The surge is attributed to the strong presence of the **Tamizhaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** across social media platforms and the popularity of Mr. Vijay himself, a celebrated actor. Officials attribute the increase to the active engagement of young followers, particularly those associated with the TVK's youth wing or IT team in various districts.

recent_articles.title: ​Split wide open: On the AIADMK, Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **AIADMK**, the principal opposition party in Tamil Nadu, is facing a split after a second consecutive election defeat.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has indicated his support for the dissident group led by former Ministers **C.Ve. Shanmugam** and **S.P. Velumani**. The dissidents have announced their intention to support the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.  The Palaniswami camp claims that all 47 legislators gave written consent for **Edappadi K. Palaniswami** as the AIADMK legislature party leader, citing a Supreme Court verdict in the Shiv Sena case. The Assembly Speaker will need to assess the merits of both groups' claims and may soon have to draw on his experience and legal advice.

recent_articles.title: The legacy of women Ministers in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, was sworn in alongside **Keerthana**, who won from the Sivakasi assembly constituency, marking a significant milestone for women in state politics.  While social media erroneously claimed she was the first woman Cabinet member, women have served as Ministers in the Tamil Nadu Cabinet for decades, with the first instance occurring in 1946 under **T. Prakasam**. Since then, women have been consistently included in the state's Cabinets.

recent_articles.title: Over 25 TASMAC outlets identified in Vellore and nearby districts for permanent closure - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tasmac**, the **Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited**, is permanently closing 25 liquor outlets in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts. The move follows a directive from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to shut down 717 Tasmac outlets within 500 meters of places of worship, educational institutions, and bus stands across the state.  The process involves identifying outlets near sensitive public spaces, with stocks being transferred to godowns and staff redeployed to other locations. The decision aims to address public concerns about proximity to these areas.

The party's manifesto promises initiatives like collateral-free education loans, a Tamil Employment Credit System, and a new post to deliver services at people's doorsteps.

recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** founder actor C. Joseph Vijay filed a petition with **Tamil Nadu Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik**, alleging selective use of the administrative machinery against the party during the election campaign.  Vijay cited numerous incidents, including denial of permission for rallies and office closures, as evidence of this alleged bias. He requested the immediate transfer of key officials and the appointment of special police observers to ensure a transparent and uniform permission system. **TVK** leader K.A. Sengottaiyan echoed these concerns, questioning "double standards" in allowing political gatherings.
